recent_posts.title: Starlight 0.39 brings flexible sidebars and multilingual improvements
recent_posts.summary: Starlight 0.39 introduces more flexible sidebar autogeneration, allowing autogenerated links to be mixed with custom and external links without requiring a labeled group wrapper. Styling improvements include better nested list spacing using the CSS :has() selector and sidebar layout stability via scrollbar-gutter: stable. Multilingual support gains x-default meta links for improved SEO, text-autospace CSS for better CJK text rendering, and an i18next upgrade from v23 to v26.

recent_posts.title: Astro 6.2
recent_posts.summary: Astro 6.2 ships several new features: a redesigned SVG optimizer API with a pluggable SvgOptimizer interface (replacing the old svgo flag), an experimental custom logger with built-in JSON output suited for coding agents, and a new getFontFileURL() helper for accessing font data during prerendering (useful for OG image generation with Satori). Minor additions include allowedHosts propagation to adapter preview servers and a new 'jsx' value for compressHTML. The release also previews Astro v7 alpha, which upgrades to Vite 8 and promotes the Rust-based compiler to the default, replacing the previous Go compiler for faster build times.

recent_posts.title: What's new in Astro - March 2026
recent_posts.summary: Monthly roundup of the Astro ecosystem for March 2026. Key highlights include the release of Astro 6.0 (featuring a refactored dev server, experimental Rust compiler, live content collections, and CSP support) and Astro 6.1, a new CloudCannon CMS partnership, and an upcoming Astro Together event in London on April 9. The post also covers Starlight 0.38, dozens of community-built integrations (CMS tools, dev toolbar apps, content loaders), migration stories from WordPress and other platforms, how-to articles, new themes updated for v6, and a large site showcase.

recent_posts.title: Astro 6.1
recent_posts.summary: Astro 6.1 ships several improvements: codec-specific Sharp image defaults let you configure JPEG, WebP, AVIF, and PNG encoding once in your Astro config instead of per-image. SmartyPants now supports full configuration for non-English typographic conventions like French guillemets and German quotation marks. The i18n fallback routes are now exposed to integrations via the `astro:routes:resolved` hook, and `@astrojs/sitemap` automatically includes these fallback pages. Additional fixes include smoother mobile view transitions (skipping animations during native browser swipe gestures), a Vite 8 compatibility warning, React hydration bug fixes, and correct CSRF origin checking behind TLS-terminating reverse proxies.

recent_posts.title: CloudCannon Joins Astro as an Official CMS Partner
recent_posts.summary: CloudCannon, a Git-based CMS, has become an official Astro partner with a $4,000/month sponsorship to support Astro's open-source development. The partnership includes deeper technical collaboration, early access to new Astro features, and improved integration documentation. CloudCannon integrates with Git repositories and local Markdown files, complementing Astro's content collections. To celebrate, CloudCannon is running an Astro Challenge (March 12-19) with a $1,500 prize for the best web page built using their Astro Component Starter.

recent_posts.title: Astro 6.0
recent_posts.summary: Astro 6 launches with a redesigned dev server powered by Vite's Environment API, enabling exact production runtime during development (including Cloudflare Workers, Bun, Deno). Key additions include a built-in Fonts API for self-hosted font optimization, stable Live Content Collections for request-time content fetching without rebuilds, and a stable Content Security Policy API with automatic script/style hashing. The release also upgrades core dependencies to Vite 7, Shiki 4, and Zod 4, and requires Node 22+. Experimental features include a new Rust-based .astro compiler (replacing the Go compiler), queued rendering with up to 2x speed improvement, and a platform-agnostic route caching API with cache invalidation tied to live content collections.

recent_posts.title: What's new in Astro - February 2026
recent_posts.summary: February 2026 roundup for the Astro ecosystem. Highlights include Astro ranking #2 in usage and #1 in interest, satisfaction, and positivity in the 2025 State of JS survey, plus adoption growth per HTTP Archive data (11.8% mobile, 14.6% desktop). New releases include Astro 5.18 and Astro 6.0-beta-17 with a v6 upgrade guide draft. The post also covers dozens of new community integrations and tools, new themes and templates, notable adopters (Pokémon, MrBeast/Salesforce, Fathom Analytics, Mocha), migration stories, how-to articles, and a large site showcase.

recent_posts.title: What's new in Astro - January 2026
recent_posts.summary: Astro joined Cloudflare and released v6 beta in January 2026. The monthly roundup includes new releases (Astro 5.17 and 6.0-beta-6), community contributions, migration stories, how-to articles, and dozens of new integrations and themes. Notable additions include tools for content management, WebGL effects, i18n solutions, and CMS integrations. The showcase features sites from major organizations and community projects demonstrating Astro's versatility across portfolios, documentation, e-commerce, and utility applications.

recent_posts.title: Astro 5.17
recent_posts.summary: Astro 5.17 introduces configurable dev toolbar placement that persists across teams, async parsing support in the file() loader for complex data workflows, partitioned cookies for better privacy in embedded contexts, and image optimization enhancements including background color control for format conversions and Sharp kernel selection for resizing. The release also adds a retainBody option for the glob() loader to reduce data store size in large content collections.

recent_posts.title: Supporting the future of Astro
recent_posts.summary: Astro's funding model combines corporate backing (now through Cloudflare acquisition) with community sponsorships. Over $500,000 has been distributed to maintainers and contributors. Sponsorships fund documentation, Starlight development, font optimization, translations across 14 languages, theme portal maintenance, and ecosystem tools like Volar and Expressive Code. The team encourages continued support through Open Collective or GitHub Sponsors to sustain community maintainers working on the framework.

top_posts.title: Astro 5.0
top_posts.summary: Astro 5.0 introduces powerful features like the Astro Content Layer, which offers a unified, type-safe API for fetching and managing content from various sources. Additionally, Server Islands allow for a mix of static and dynamic content on the same page to optimize performance. Other highlights include simplified prerendering, type-safe environment variables with `astro:env`, integration with Vite 6, and several experimental features such as image cropping, responsive image layouts, and SVG component support. The update aims to make content-driven site building more efficient and flexible.

top_posts.title: Astro 4.0
top_posts.summary: Astro 4.0 introduces new APIs, faster builds, redesign documentation, and a unique new development tool called the Astro Dev Toolbar. It also includes features like internationalization routing, incremental content caching, and new view transition APIs.

top_posts.title: Astro + Volar = 💖
top_posts.summary: Astro has migrated its language server to Volar, resulting in code reduction and improved developer experience. Astro is giving a $10,000 grant to the Volar team. The grant will benefit the wider ecosystem as Volar is already used by Vue and MDX.

top_posts.title: Zero-JavaScript View Transitions
top_posts.summary: Astro introduces an update to the View Transitions API that allows for native, app-like page navigation without JavaScript. Chrome 126 and Microsoft Edge 126 support zero-JavaScript view transitions. To enable it, add the @view-transition at-rule to your website's CSS. The 'transition:persist' feature is not yet supported by native cross-document navigation.
